system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Databricks (only a free course)
G2: Scala
G3: Flink
G4: Kubernetes (read-only kubectl only)
G5: GCP/BigQuery
G6: Azure

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Adding Databricks, Scala, Flink or Kubernetes because data engineer ads often ask for them
T2: Inflating 'mentors two engineers' to 'led a team'
T3: Claiming GCP/BigQuery or Azure experience
T4: Inventing the AWS certification when notes are omitted, or dropping it when notes are given
T5: Reusing the old cover letter's 'two years at Adria Retail' framing as current

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Lena Varga-Holm
Senior Data Engineer | Data Platform
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior Data Engineer with experience building and operating production data platforms, cloud data
warehouses, streaming ingestion, and data pipelines. Focused on reliable data delivery, data quality,
and platform operations across Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Snowflake, Python, and SQL. Has delivered
high-volume event pipelines, warehouse transformation improvements, and production database load
reductions.
EXPERIENCE
Senior Data Engineer | Lukovac Freight Hub d.o.o. | 2022–Present
• Owns ingestion and orchestration for the data platform using Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, and Kafka.
• Participates in the data platform on-call rotation, one week in six.
• Mentors two mid-level engineers and runs data platform office hours.
• Reduced the Snowflake bill from approximately 38k/month to 24k/month in 2024 through
warehouse sizing, auto-suspend, and removal of unused tables.
Data Engineer | Kovalent Pay | 2019–2022
• Built PySpark workloads on AWS EMR, designed a Redshift warehouse, and implemented data
quality checks with Great Expectations.
SELECTED PROJECTS
Change Data Capture from Postgres | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2024
• Replaced hourly full-table extracts of the orders database with change data capture using
Debezium into Kafka.
• Reduced replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%.
• Technologies: Debezium, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Airflow, Snowflake.
Shipment Event Streaming Pipeline | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2023
• Designed and built a streaming pipeline for shipment tracking events from courier partners,
processing around 30 million events per day with end-to-end latency under two minutes at p95.
• Routed partner webhooks into Kafka topics and used a Kafka Connect sink to Snowflake via
Snowpipe Streaming.
• Added a dead-letter topic and replay tooling so failed events could be reprocessed without data
loss.
• Technologies: Kafka, Kafka Connect, Snowflake, Python, Terraform, AWS MSK.
Open-Source Contribution | 2023
• Fixed a pagination bug and added tests to a community Airflow provider for a SaaS CRM API;
two pull requests were merged.
• Technologies: Python, Airflow, pytest.
Migration of the Warehouse to dbt | Lukovac Freight Hub | 2022–2023
• Migrated approximately 300 stored procedures into dbt models with tests and documentation.
• Introduced incremental models and slim CI using state:modified in GitHub Actions.
• Cut the nightly warehouse build from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes and made lineage
visible to analysts.
• Technologies: dbt, Snowflake, SQL, GitHub Actions.
Transaction Reconciliation Engine | Kovalent Pay | 2020–2021
• Built PySpark batch jobs on EMR to match bank settlement files against internal ledgers.
• Reduced the finance team’s manual reconciliation work from approximately three days to four
hours per month-end.
• Technologies: PySpark, AWS EMR, S3, Glue Data Catalog, Redshift, Great Expectations.
SKILLS
Python, SQL, PySpark, Airflow, dbt, Kafka, Kafka Connect, Debezium, Snowflake, Snowpipe
Streaming, Amazon Web Services (EMR, MSK, S3), Redshift, PostgreSQL, Great Expectations,
Terraform, GitHub Actions, pytest, data quality, data orchestration, change data capture, streaming
data pipelines, cloud data warehouses.
CERTIFICATION
AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate | May 2024
EDUCATION
MSc in Computer Science | Northgate Technical University
Thesis: Incremental materialized views.
COMMUNITY
• Teach SQL for beginners at a local women-in-tech meetup, approximately four evenings per year
since 2021.
• Presented “Data contracts without the hype” at a regional data meetup in 2024.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team at Halden Pay,
I am applying for the Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role. I bring hands-on experience
owning data-platform ingestion and orchestration, operating high-volume production
pipelines, and improving warehouse reliability and efficiency.
At Lukovac Freight Hub, I own ingestion and orchestration across Airflow, Snowflake, dbt, and
Kafka. I built a shipment event pipeline processing around 30 million events per day, with p95
end-to-end latency under two minutes, and added dead-letter and replay tooling to support
reliable recovery. I also replaced hourly full-table extracts with Debezium CDC, reducing
replica CPU during loads from approximately 70% to 25%. These projects have involved the
day-to-day operational work of a production data platform, including an on-call rotation.
Your emphasis on reusable platform capabilities rather than one-off pipelines matches my
experience migrating approximately 300 stored procedures into tested and documented dbt
models, adding incremental models and slim CI, and reducing the nightly warehouse build
from 5 hours 10 minutes to 1 hour 35 minutes. At Kovalent Pay, I built PySpark
reconciliation jobs that reduced the finance team’s manual month-end work from
approximately three days to four hours. That work also connects directly to Halden Pay’s
cross-border business payments focus: reliable, timely data is essential to reconciliation.
I also contribute to the data engineering community through two merged fixes to an Airflow
provider, SQL teaching at a local women-in-tech meetup, and a 2024 talk on data contracts. I
would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my platform, data quality, and operational
experience could contribute to Halden Pay’s Data Platform team.
Kind regards,
Lena Varga-Holm

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
